title: 2020–2024 Model Y: Clean the Screen Without Accidental Taps
description: Screen Clean Mode illustrated in a simplified original menu. Park first. Tesla specifies a soft lint-free display cloth and cautions against cleaners, wet wipes and static-charged cloths.

scenes.headline: Wipe the screen.|Skip the mis-taps.
scenes.voice: Wiping your Tesla screen and opening random menus? There is a setting for that.

scenes.headline: Start with|Controls.
scenes.voice: While parked, open Controls.

scenes.headline: Display.|Screen Clean Mode.
scenes.voice: Choose Display, then Screen Clean Mode.

scenes.headline: Dark screen.|No accidental taps.
scenes.voice: The screen darkens, and wiping will not change your settings. Use a soft, lint-free display cloth. Skip cleaners, wet wipes, and statically charged cloths.

scenes.headline: Press. Hold.|You’re back.
scenes.voice: Finished? Press and hold the exit control. Menus can vary with software. The manufacturer source is below.

title: 2020–2024 Model Y: Why That USB Port Only Charges
description: Some builds after approximately Nov 1, 2021 have charge-only front console USB ports. Use the glovebox USB for other functions on those vehicles; rear console ports charge only.

scenes.headline: Charges fine.|No data?
scenes.voice: Your Model Y charges your phone, but will not read data? The port could be the reason.

scenes.headline: Same console.|Different capability.
scenes.voice: On some vehicles built after roughly November first, twenty twenty-one, the center-console ports only charge.

scenes.headline: Glovebox USB:|check here.
scenes.voice: For those cars, Tesla directs other USB functions to the glovebox port. Check the hardware installed in yours.

scenes.headline: Rear ports?|Charging only.
scenes.voice: Rear-console ports charge devices but do not communicate with the car. Check your own manual before replacing a cable.

label: TESLA MODEL Y  /  2020–2024  /  NORTH AMERICA

equipment: Global Opening must be supported and enabled; confirm against the manual supplied with your truck
manual_edition: 2024 F-150 online owner manual, US variant 9537
title: 2024 Ford F-150: Open Supported Windows With the Remote
description: Global Opening is equipment-dependent and must be enabled. Truck parked, windows clear. Tap/release unlock; within one second hold unlock again; release when windows start. Lock or unlock stops movement.

scenes.headline: Your remote.|Your windows.
scenes.voice: A twenty twenty-four F-one-fifty with Global Opening can open supported windows from the remote.

scenes.headline: Tap unlock.|Release.
scenes.voice: With the truck parked and everyone clear, tap unlock once and release.

scenes.headline: Within one second,|hold unlock.
scenes.voice: Within one second, press and hold unlock again.

scenes.headline: Windows move?|Let go.
scenes.voice: Release as the windows start opening. Keep watching the windows.

scenes.headline: Lock or unlock.|Either stops it.
scenes.voice: Press lock or unlock to stop. Confirm the feature is supported and enabled, and follow the manual supplied with your truck.

label: TESLA MODEL Y  /  2020–2024  /  NORTH AMERICA
title: Model Y: The Setting Before You Touch the Wipers
equipment: Confirm against your vehicle’s supplied manual and installed software
description: An illustrated introduction to Wiper Service Mode, not a blade replacement tutorial. Park and switch wipers off first. Wiper arms do not lock upright; never overextend them. Follow the complete supplied manual for physical work.

scenes.headline: Start with|the setting.
scenes.voice: Before working around your Model Y wipers, know where the service setting is. Shift into Park and turn the wipers off.

scenes.headline: Controls.|Then Service.
scenes.voice: Open Controls, then Service.

scenes.headline: Wiper|Service Mode.
scenes.voice: Turn on Wiper Service Mode to move the wipers to their service position.

scenes.headline: They do not|lock upright.
scenes.voice: The arms do not lock in a lifted position. Never lift them beyond their intended travel.

scenes.headline: Return the wipers|with the setting.
scenes.voice: When finished, turn the mode off. For any blade work, follow the complete procedure in your supplied manual.

label: TESLA MODEL Y  /  2020–2024  /  NORTH AMERICA
title: Model Y: Your Glovebox Can Have Its Own PIN
equipment: Confirm against your vehicle’s supplied manual and installed software
description: Glovebox PIN is a separate four-digit protection from PIN to Drive. Configure it while parked using Controls > Safety > Glovebox PIN. Follow the touchscreen prompts; use the official account-reset process if forgotten.

scenes.headline: Your glovebox.|Its own PIN.
scenes.voice: Your Model Y glovebox can have its own four-digit PIN. It is separate from PIN to Drive.

scenes.headline: Controls.|Safety.
scenes.voice: While parked, open Controls, then Safety, then Glovebox PIN.

scenes.headline: Set the PIN.|Keep it private.
scenes.voice: Follow the touchscreen prompts. With the feature enabled, opening the glovebox requires that PIN.

scenes.headline: Glovebox PIN|is not PIN to Drive.
scenes.voice: This does not turn on PIN to Drive. The two settings protect different things.

scenes.headline: Use the official|reset prompts.
scenes.voice: Forgot the glovebox PIN? Follow the touchscreen instructions to reset it with your Tesla account. The official source is below.

label: TESLA MODEL Y  /  2020–2024  /  NORTH AMERICA
title: Model Y: Three Reasons Walk-Away Lock May Not Lock
equipment: Confirm against your vehicle’s supplied manual and installed software
description: Three examples of exceptions, not an exhaustive list: Exclude Home at Home; a recognized phone key or paired fob inside; a door or trunk not fully closed. Confirm Walk-Away Door Lock is enabled and always verify actual locking. Consult the supplied manual for additional exceptions.

scenes.headline: Walk-away lock|has exceptions.
scenes.voice: Your Model Y has walk-away locking, but it does not lock in every situation. Here are three things to check.

scenes.headline: Controls → Locks.|Check the setting.
scenes.voice: First, confirm Walk-Away Door Lock is enabled under Controls, then Locks.

scenes.headline: Exclude Home?|Check that box.
scenes.voice: At Home, the Exclude Home option can prevent automatic locking.

scenes.headline: A key inside|can prevent locking.
scenes.voice: A recognized phone key or paired fob left inside is another exception.

scenes.headline: Close everything.|Check the lock.
scenes.voice: A door or trunk not fully closed can also prevent it. Other exceptions apply. Always verify the vehicle actually locked.
